title: Those Who Kept the Watch
acceptance:
Mara's neighbors reached Lanternhold, but the wardens buried beside the eastern road have not been allowed to rest. The courier's seal has turned their old watch into a command: let nobody leave.

Defeat 40 Skeletons of level 3 or higher in Earth. Begin along the roads just beyond Lanternhold; you need not reach the distant burial grounds to break the watch. Listen to their bound echoes. We must learn how the command travels before asking the grove to surrender its Memory Seeds.
completion:
Their last duty was to keep a road open. Malachar made that same duty close it. Even a loving promise can become a prison when somebody else claims the right to define it.

The echoes weaken between the roots. Gather the Verdant Memory Seeds next; those living memories can tell Maelin what the wardens were protecting before the seal rewrote their watch.
handoff: Mara got her neighbors out, and her diary tells us the roots were redirected, not simply weakened. The dead wardens still repeat the courier's order along the road. We must break that watch and study its echoes before gathering the grove's memories.
lore: Earth's wardens swore to preserve passage, not possession. The first counter-covenant reversed the meaning of their oath while leaving its words intact.
catchupAcceptance: The Bastion road is already behind your journey, but its bound wardens still reveal how the courier corrupted an oath. Investigate their echoes if you wish; this expedition will not hold back your main story.
catchupCompletion: You have recorded what happened to the wardens without pretending the road must be won again. Their story belongs beside Mara's, not beneath Malachar's account of it.

title: Ink That Walks
acceptance:
The Seeds remember rain and patient hands. Yet the wound writes over that memory each night. The Imps west of Lanternhold carry the courier's burning script from root to root.

Defeat 60 level-20-or-higher Imps in Earth. These are not repair fragments to gather: their passing echoes will let me separate the repeated command from the grove's own voice. Then compare the three records at the returning scar.
completion:
Each echo repeats the same instruction: shelter belongs to the obedient. It is not Orun speaking. It is a sentence being copied until the land can hear nothing else.

Now study the severed root, the new growth and the marked stone. We can recognize the foreign words without tearing away the memory beneath them.
handoff: There is a forest older than language inside these Seeds. I will keep them for Maelin's Vigil. Before we examine the scar, silence the Imps carrying its command through the western roots; their echoes will help us recognize what the mark is rewriting.
lore: The courier needed no army to speak every command himself. He taught lesser creatures a repeating script and let the wounded land distribute it.
catchupAcceptance: You already know the scar's meaning. The Imps still carry examples of its repeating script; recording them is optional research, not a new lock on the Bastion road.
catchupCompletion: The surviving script confirms what the scar taught us. Repetition gave the lie its reach, never its truth.

title: The Borrowed Oath
acceptance:
The fifth incision interrupts every part of the covenant. Its seal points toward the Bastion, but the Demon Orcs east of Lanternhold carry lesser copies of the Sentinel's order.

Defeat 50 level-30-or-higher Demon Orcs in Earth. Their echoes will reveal the cadence that holds the root-road shut. Check your equipment and spend your earned training points before facing them; the dungeon will demand at least this much preparation.
completion:
The cadence ends where an answer should begin. Malachar wants an oath with no second voice, a guardian who can never ask whether an order still protects anyone.

We can now recognize that binding inside the Hollow Sentinel. Clear the whole Verdant Bastion Catacombs to open the deeper raid-road. The Guide still requires level 30, and the Rootheart itself still needs Maelin's defended Vigil.
handoff: The scar repeats a false oath, while the Seeds preserve the original covenant. Before entering the Bastion, study the binding carried by its Demon Orcs. We must recognize the Sentinel's command without mistaking an opened road for a repaired crystal.
lore: Orun's oldest oaths left space for an answer. The counter-covenant removed that space, turning guardianship into obedience.
catchupAcceptance: The Sentinel's road is already open to you. Its surviving oath-bearers can still teach us about the binding; this is an optional expedition, not a demand to earn that access twice.
catchupCompletion: Their echoes preserve the shape of the command you have already overcome. I have added them to the Chronicle without rewriting your victory.

title: The Ferry That Never Came
acceptance:
The Rootheart raid-road is open, not repaired. While we prepare the other roads, Neris's distress is reaching us through the wells. Supplies for Dain's flood shelter never arrived: the old Constructs in western Earth still enforce a transit order bearing the courier's seal.

Defeat 60 level-40-or-higher Constructs in Earth. Their command echoes will show why a route meant to carry aid became a border nobody could cross. Then find Dain's ledger in Water's abandoned flood shelter.
completion:
The order did not forbid the ferry. It required permission from a name the courier had already erased. A perfect little prison: every keeper could claim to be following the rules.

Go to Dain's shelter in Water. His ledger may preserve the people behind the missing names, and why Neris could no longer carry them home.
handoff: The Sentinel's oath is free, and Orun has shown us the deeper raid-road. The crystal remains wounded. Before we follow Water's call, trace the missing relief ferry through the Constructs in western Earth; the courier used our own routes to isolate the next realm.
lore: Malachar's sealed transit orders often demanded authorization from people his other spells had erased. He made abandonment look like a lawful duty.
catchupAcceptance: You have already followed Water's story beyond the missing ferry. Its transit orders remain useful evidence, but this optional Earth expedition cannot take that progress away.
catchupCompletion: A name removed from a ledger is still a person. The recovered orders show how deliberately Malachar confused those two things.

title: Debts Beneath the Snow
acceptance:
Dain recorded crossings, not debts. The Mountain Trolls along Water's southern snowfields have been bound to a different accounting: every sheltered life must be repaid to a master.

Defeat 60 level-50-or-higher Mountain Trolls in Water. Compare the echoes they release with the shelter's record. We need to separate Neris's freely kept promises from the courier's claim that kindness creates ownership.
completion:
Their bindings count rescue as a purchase. Dain never asked the people on his ferry to belong to him. That difference is the thread Malachar could not make disappear.

Gather the Moon-Tide Pearls next. Maelin will need their returning rhythm when we finally reach the Tidestar itself.
handoff: Dain's ledger preserves people, not property. The Trolls beyond the shelter carry bindings that turn those crossings into debts. Study their echoes before gathering the Pearls, so we know which promises still belong to Neris.
lore: Neris remembers a promise because it joins two lives. The counter-covenant recast that bond as a debt payable forever to a third.
catchupAcceptance: The shelter has already guided you onward. The Trolls' bindings remain an optional account of how its promises were distorted; your main journey need not wait for it.
catchupCompletion: The echoes disagree with Dain's ledger exactly where mercy should have been. We now have both records, and need not let the crueler one speak alone.

title: A Current Without a Master
acceptance:
The echo pools reveal what was taken from the reflection. Aqua Golems farther north carry the same interruption through the channels feeding the Well.

Defeat 70 level-55-or-higher Aqua Golems in Water. Their echoes will let me follow the stolen route-name into Thalorath's undertow. The Pearls remain with me for Maelin; these echoes prepare the descent, not the crystal's repair.
completion:
There is a pause in every echo where a name should return. Thalorath did not destroy the route. He made the water forget whom it was allowed to carry.

Clear the entire Abyssal Well and reclaim the drowned name. The Guide requires level 60. Beyond the dungeon lies Neris's separate raid sanctum; only its full Vigil can restore the Tidestar.
handoff: The pools and mooring bell reveal the missing name without surrendering the memory around it. Follow that interruption through the Aqua Golems' echoes before entering the Well. Then we can confront Thalorath knowing what must be returned.
lore: A route-name was once an invitation shared between water and traveler. Malachar tried to turn it into a password only his servants could remember.
catchupAcceptance: The Well's route-name is already part of your Chronicle. The Golems still carry fragments of its interruption; studying them is optional and does not reseal the Confluence.
catchupCompletion: The recovered pauses now sit beside the restored name. The Chronicle remembers the wound without treating it as the world's permanent shape.

title: Fuel for an Unending War
acceptance:
The kiln's record shows why Pyralis's purpose mattered. Its fire could finish a task and rest. The Magma Golems farther west carry a command with no word for enough.

Defeat 35 level-75-or-higher Magma Golems in Fire. Record their command echoes, then gather Cinderheart Ore. We must give Maelin a memory of useful flame, not merely a hotter weapon.
completion:
Each command names another enemy before the last has fallen. An endless war needs no victory; it needs only people too afraid to let its furnaces cool.

Gather the Cinderheart Ore. We will keep the kiln's older purpose alive while we investigate the command anchor and seek Infernax's furnace-key.
handoff: The kiln's record remembers flame that warmed, shaped and finally rested. The Magma Golems repeat a command that cannot end. Study that command before collecting the Ore, so our repair preserves purpose instead of feeding another war.
lore: Pyralis's covenant allowed a fire to end when its work was done. Malachar removed the ending and called the resulting hunger strength.
catchupAcceptance: You have already carried Fire's story forward. The Golems' unending orders remain optional evidence; you need not repeat your furnace-key victory to study them.
catchupCompletion: Their orders reveal no goal beyond the next battle. We will remember the kiln's finished work as carefully as its flame.

title: The Hours We Refuse to Lose
acceptance:
The station's record holds a future its instruments were forbidden to show. Thunder Rocs in the eastern heights carry the repeated interval that keeps the storm turning back.

Defeat 30 level-80-or-higher Thunder Rocs in Air. Their echoes will help us hear the missing beat before we gather the Stormglass Pinions. Aeral's freedom is not an absence of direction; it is the right to choose another one.
completion:
The missing beat is not silence. It is the moment in which a choice could have been made. Malachar steals that moment and calls the remaining repetition peace.

Gather the Stormglass Pinions, each with its own thunderclap. Then study the vane, updraft and free marker before confronting Zephyrion's loop.
handoff: The station's record preserves the possibility of a different tomorrow. Trace the repeated interval through the Thunder Rocs before collecting the Pinions. We must learn to hear a choice the storm has tried to erase.
lore: Aeral's covenant did not promise a world without storms. It promised that no storm could own every direction a life might take.
catchupAcceptance: You have already moved beyond the station's warning. The Rocs still carry the stolen interval; this optional expedition adds context without taking away your path to the Eyrie.
catchupCompletion: The interval is recorded, and so is the choice that follows it. Repetition can imprison a moment, but it cannot make that moment the whole sky.
